cases.title: WebSocket Media Streaming Timeout - 422 Error 90046
cases.findings:
**Issue:** WebSocket media streaming fails with 422 / error 90046 "Failed to connect to destination".

**Engineering Finding:** WebSocket takes ~4.5s to establish → exceeds call control timeout.

**Customer Rebuttal:** App is warm, handshake completes ~2.5-3s, but 422 returns before handshake finishes.

**Customer Ask:** Increase media streaming timeout for number +3677201027.
cases.notes: ENGDESK: 50333. Sean pushed back to engineering with customer's rebuttal (03-26).
cases.response: Engineering investigating timeout discrepancy. Customer reports handshake completes faster than measured.

cases.title: Hangup Source Discrepancy - UI vs Buyer Perspective
cases.findings:
**Issue:** Conflicting hangup source — UI shows "target hung up" but buyer shows "caller hung up".

**Root Cause:** Perspective difference — Twilio/buyer disconnected first, but from their view Telnyx is the "caller".

**Explanation:** When Ringba transfers to buyer via Twilio, the buyer sees Telnyx/Ringba as the originator. If buyer hangs up, from their CDRs it's "caller" (Ringba) that caused disconnection, but from Ringba's view, the "target" (buyer) hung up.
cases.notes: Customer education case — explained perspective difference in call flow.
cases.response: Explained perspective difference: both views are correct from different vantage points in the call flow.

cases.title: SMS Segment Count vs Display - Customer Education
cases.findings:
**Issue:** Customer confused why 2 SMS segments display as 1 message on recipient device.

**Explanation:** UDH (User Data Header) enables device reassembly. Segments are transport-level; display is unified by recipient device.

**Key Facts:**
- GSM-7: 160 chars single / 153 chars per multipart segment
- UTF-16: 70 chars single / 67 chars per multipart segment
- Billing is per segment, display is unified
cases.notes: Cited Telnyx documentation for accuracy.
cases.response: Explained UDH-based segment reassembly with Telnyx doc references.

cases.title: PSTN numbers appearing as SIP calls
cases.findings:
**Root Cause:** Customer's Call Control application webhook logic was transforming destinations to SIP URIs (LiveKit endpoints) - not Telnyx infrastructure.

**Key Detail:** Calls route through Vocara's Call Control app (account `e90489f7-ebd8-4f10-bfa7-73d5a43d5489`) which transforms PSTN destinations to LiveKit SIP URIs on transfer leg.

**Call Samples Analyzed:**
- 71a2a3d2-1efa-11f1-b6af-02420aef50a0
- e19ebbd2-219b-11f1-b28e-02420aef3ca0

**Conclusion:** Application-level behavior in customer webhook, not automatic Telnyx conversion.
cases.notes: Customer initially claimed Telnyx was converting PSTN to SIP. Analysis showed Vocara webhook logic was the source.
cases.response: Explained this is application-level behavior in Vocara's Call Control app, not Telnyx automatic conversion.

cases.title: T.38/G.711 race condition - Fax failures to toll-free
cases.findings:
**Issue:** Unable to send fax to +1 866-288-4455 (toll-free), ongoing 15 days.

**Root Cause:** T.38/G.711 race condition
- Call starts with G.711 PCMU audio passthrough
- During V.17/V.29 fax modem training, carrier sends T.38 re-INVITE
- Switchover mid-training causes T.30 handshake desync
- Session stalls, carrier times out

**Resolution Applied:**
- Disabled T.38 on Fax API connection via private API
- Connection ID: 2153687997793437157
- API Response: {"changes":"applied"}
cases.notes:
Customer can't disable T.38 themselves for Fax API connections - requires server-side fix via private API.

Learning: Fax API T.38 toggle endpoint: http://faxes.service.ch1b-prod.consul:4014/private/v2/admin/connection_settings
cases.response: T.38 disabled on connection. Awaiting customer retest to confirm resolution.

cases.title: MS Teams Call Me drops after ~40 seconds (RTP No-Op handling)
cases.findings:
**Root Cause:** Customer's AudioCodes SBC sends RTP No-Op packets (PT=120, payload 00000000) as keepalives when no audio is flowing. Carrier (Verizon Wireless) terminates with RTP-RTCP Timeout despite Telnyx forwarding transcoded packets.

**Call Pattern:**
- 0-8 sec: No-Ops sent (call setup)
- 9-14 sec: G.729 audio (IVR prompt plays)
- 15+ sec: Only No-Ops at 1/sec (audio stops)
- ~40-48 sec: Carrier BYE with RTP-RTCP Timeout

**PCAP Analysis:**
- Sample 1: 39 No-Op packets (frames 116, 217, 318...)
- Sample 2: 34 No-Op packets (frames 115, 216, 1338...)
- Telnyx B2BUA transcodes to AMR-WB (PT=102) and forwards
- Carrier still terminates despite receiving continuous RTP

**Key Question:** What does B2BUA generate when receiving PT=120 No-Op with zero payload?
cases.notes:
VIP account - 2+ months ongoing.

Wireshark filter: rtp.p_type == 120

Escalated to internal engineering team 2026-03-16.
cases.response: Escalated internally. Investigating how B2BUA handles RTP No-Op packets (PT=120). Will update when we have findings.

cases.title: Zambia SIM connectivity - 0 bytes transferred, uplink broken
cases.findings:
**Issue:** SIMs in Zambia connect with good signal but get virtually no data throughput.

**ICCIDs:**
- 89311210000005412490 (original)
- 89311210000006059191 (new report)

**WDR Analysis (99 sessions):**
- 60% showed 0 bytes transferred
- 35% showed <1KB downlink only, 0 uplink
- Only 1 session out of 99 had bidirectional data

**Root Cause:** Bearer path / GTP-U tunnel issue between Sparkle roaming platform and Airtel Zambia (MCC 645 / MNC 01). PDP context activates but data plane is broken.
cases.notes:
Pattern: PSSGW events with 0 bytes = signaling works, data plane broken.

Escalation doc prepared for Sparkle.
cases.response: Data analysis confirms systematic uplink failure on Airtel Zambia. Escalating to Sparkle for GTP-U tunnel investigation.

cases.title: Conferencing Issue: Caller can't get back to original caller
cases.findings:
**Pattern identified across all 3 examples:**
Agent leg disconnects before conference dial-out completes, leaving original caller stranded.

**Call a7cfa766 timeline:**
- 19:24:02 — Agent bridged to caller
- 19:28:09 — Agent leg disconnected
- 19:30:35 — Conference dial-outs initiated (2+ min after agent gone)
- 19:30:53 — Conference targets answered but never bridged
- 19:32:52 — Original caller hung up after 4+ min alone

**Root Cause:** Call Control flow timing issue — conference dial-outs created after agent has disconnected.
cases.notes:
Customer-side Call Control implementation issue, not a Telnyx platform bug.

Asked customer:
1. What triggers agent leg hangup?
2. Is there webhook handling to prevent conference initiation if agent is gone?
cases.response: Analysis complete. Agent leg disconnects before conference completes. This is a Call Control flow timing issue in customer implementation.
